faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.subtitle: Clear answers about accounts, learning paths, exams, interviews, friends, and AI on AlefYa.
faq.homeSub: Start here — or open the full FAQ for every topic.

whatIsAlefya.a: AlefYa is a bilingual learning platform that takes you from Alef to Ya — ordered tracks, stage exams, interview practice, and progress saved to your account.

bilingual.q: Is the site available in Arabic and English?
bilingual.a: Yes. Use the language switcher in the header anytime. Content, UI, and learning materials are built for both Arabic and English.

isFree.a: You can explore categories and start learning with a free account. Core learning paths, progress, exams, and interview prep are available after you sign up.

whereToStart.q: Where should I start if I’m new?
whereToStart.a: Open From zero to build a personal plan, or browse Categories if you already know your field. Both routes lead into ordered tracks.

whoIsItFor.a: Complete beginners, learners who know some basics, and people returning to coding who want a clear specialization path with checkpoints.

needAccount.a: Browsing is open, but saving a roadmap, tracking lessons, taking exams, messaging friends, and using your dashboard require signing up.

usernameRules.a: Usernames must be 5–32 characters: English letters, numbers, and underscores only. They are unique across the platform.

passwordRules.q: What makes a strong password here?
passwordRules.a: Use at least 8 characters with uppercase, lowercase, a number, and a special character. You can change your password anytime in Profile.

changeLevel.q: Can I change my learning level later?
changeLevel.a: Yes. After you create a From zero plan once, you can update your learning level from Profile.

publicProfile.q: What do others see on my public profile?
publicProfile.a: Everyone can see your username and friend count. Detailed track progress is visible to you and your friends only.

deleteAccount.q: How do I delete my account?
deleteAccount.a: Open Profile → Delete account. You’ll confirm with your password and username. This permanently removes progress, exams, and messages.

whatIsFromZero.a: A short wizard that asks for your level, field, language, and framework, then builds an ordered plan starting with language fundamentals.

howPlanBuilt.q: How is my learning plan built?
howPlanBuilt.a: We always start with a language track, then the framework track. You move lesson by lesson, with a stage exam after each phase.

changeFieldLater.q: Can I switch field or framework later?
changeFieldLater.a: You can explore other categories anytime. Your saved From zero plan keeps your primary path; start additional tracks from Categories when you’re ready.

resumeProgress.q: Will I resume where I left off?
resumeProgress.a: Yes. Your dashboard and From zero continue from the first unfinished lesson or exam in your plan sequence.

roadmapAiHelp.q: Can AI help me choose in From zero?
roadmapAiHelp.a: Yes. At each wizard step you can ask the roadmap helper about fields, languages, and frameworks before you commit.

lessonOrder.q: Do I have to follow lessons in order?
lessonOrder.a: Yes on a track. Lessons unlock in sequence so foundations come before advanced topics and stage exams.

progressSaved.a: When you’re signed in, completed lessons and exam results are stored on your account and sync across sessions.

lockedLessons.a: You need to finish earlier lessons (and pass the previous stage exam when required) before the next block opens.

categoriesVsTracks.q: What’s the difference between categories and tracks?
categoriesVsTracks.a: Categories group a field (e.g. frontend). Tracks are ordered Alef-to-Ya paths inside a category (language, then framework).

myTracks.q: Where do I see tracks I’ve started?
myTracks.a: Open My tracks or My Progress (dashboard) to continue enrollments and see how far you’ve gone.

whenExam.a: After you complete the lessons in a stage. The exam checks that stage before you unlock the next one.

passScore.q: What score do I need to pass an exam?
passScore.a: You need at least 75% to pass a stage exam and continue on the track.

retryExam.q: Can I retry an exam if I fail?
retryExam.a: Yes. Review the feedback, revisit lessons if needed, then take the exam again when you’re ready.

writtenQuestions.q: Are there written answers, not only multiple choice?
writtenQuestions.a: Yes. Some exams include written questions. Answers are analyzed to give you a clearer learning report.

examReport.q: What is the exam learning report?
examReport.a: After you submit, you get feedback on strengths and gaps so you know what to practice before moving on.

whatAreInterviews.a: Practice randomized interview-style questions per track, with explanations after every answer — separate from stage exams.

interviewDifficulty.a: Yes. Pick junior, mid, senior, or mixed before you start a session.

interviewExplanations.q: Do I get explanations for interview answers?
interviewExplanations.a: Yes. Every question includes a clear explanation so you learn why an answer is strong or weak.

interviewRandom.q: Are interview questions the same every time?
interviewRandom.a: No. Sessions draw from a large bank so you can practice fresh mixes for the same track.

interviewVsExam.q: How is interview prep different from stage exams?
interviewVsExam.a: Stage exams gate your track progress. Interview prep is optional practice for real interview scenarios and judgment.

howFriends.a: Send a friend request from a public profile or classmates list. Accepted friends can see more of each other’s learning progress and message freely.

friendRequestRules.q: What happens if a friend request is declined?
friendRequestRules.a: The sender cannot send another request to that person. Only the person who declined can send a request in the other direction.

howMessages.a: Message friends from Friends or their profile. You can also message classmates on a shared track. Chats open under Messages.

deleteMessage.q: Can I delete a chat message?
deleteMessage.a: Yes. On your own message, open the delete action. Both sides see “This message was deleted.”

notifications.a: The bell next to the logo. Tap a notification to open Friends requests or the related profile. You can accept or decline requests from the list too.

lessonAi.q: What is the lesson AI helper?
lessonAi.a: On lessons you can open the AI helper to ask clarifying questions about the current material without leaving the page.

aiWhatToAsk.q: What should I ask the AI helper?
aiWhatToAsk.a: Ask about concepts in the lesson, examples, comparisons, or “why this order?” Avoid pasting unrelated homework unrelated to the track.

aiLimits.q: Are there limits to AI help?
aiLimits.a: AI is a study assistant, not a replacement for reading lessons or taking exams. Replies may be unavailable if the service is busy — try again shortly.

aiGrading.q: Does AI grade my written exam answers?
aiGrading.a: Written answers can be analyzed to produce a learning-oriented report. Use it as guidance alongside the score and explanations.
